objectives.textEn: Temperature and thermometers: degree of hotness, related to average KE of molecules; temperature-dependent properties; calibrating a thermometer from a linear graph.
Heat as energy transferred due to a temperature difference; internal energy = random KE + PE of molecules.
Heat capacity C = Q/ΔT and specific heat capacity c = Q/(mΔT); measuring c (electrical method, method of mixtures); high c of water.
Conduction, convection and radiation; molecular account of conduction; infrared radiation; factors affecting emission and absorption of radiation (colour, texture, surface area, temperature).
Melting/freezing and boiling/condensing; melting and boiling points; heating and cooling curves.
Latent heat as PE change of molecules; specific latent heat of fusion and vaporisation ℓ = Q/m; problems.
Evaporation below the boiling point; cooling effect; factors affecting the rate; molecular explanation (qualitative).
General gas law: Boyle's law, p–T and V–T relationships, absolute zero by extrapolation, kelvin scale; pV/T = constant; pV = nRT (moles, N_A). [EXT]
Kinetic theory: ideal-gas assumptions; pV = ⅓Nm⟨c²⟩; average KE = 3RT/(2N_A); real gases at high T and low p. No derivation. [EXT]
Position, distance and displacement; scalars and vectors; s–t graphs.
Speed and velocity (average, instantaneous); v–t graphs; uniform motion. Relative velocity not required.
Acceleration from v–t graphs; a–t graphs.
Equations of uniformly accelerated motion (suvat): derive and apply.
Vertical motion under gravity: measuring g; graphs; effect of air resistance (qualitative).
Newton's First Law: inertia, mass, friction (no friction formulae).
Addition and resolution of forces, graphically and algebraically.
Newton's Second Law F = ma; free-body diagrams; net force; connected bodies (two-body and many-body problems in 1-D).
Newton's Third Law: action–reaction pairs.
Mass and weight.
Moment of a force, torque and couples; equilibrium of a rigid body with a fixed pivot; centre of gravity; non-perpendicular forces.
Path of a projectile; independence of horizontal and vertical motion; problems (no range or trajectory formulae). [EXT]
Mechanical work W = Fs cosθ.
Gravitational PE = mgh and KE = ½mv² (derivations).
Conservation of energy in a closed system, with energy losses; 2-D problems.
Power P = W/t and P = Fv; efficiency.
Linear momentum p = mv.
Change in momentum and net force F = Δp/Δt; F–t graphs (area = change in momentum).
Conservation of momentum (link to Newton's third law); elastic and inelastic collisions; 1-D problems; equal-mass elastic right-angle fork collision.
Angular velocity ω; v = ωr; centripetal acceleration a = v²/r = ω²r; identifying the force providing the centripetal force. [EXT]
Newton's law of gravitation F = GMm/r²; gravitational field strength g = GM/r²; g above a planet; orbital velocity of satellites. Kepler's laws and escape velocity not required here. [EXT]
Waves transfer energy without transferring matter; transverse and longitudinal waves; crest, trough, compression, rarefaction, phase (in phase / antiphase).
Displacement–time and displacement–distance graphs; f = 1/T; v = fλ.
Reflection and refraction of waves; refractive index in terms of wave speeds; wavefront diagrams.
Diffraction (effect of gap width) and interference of two coherent sources; path-difference conditions.
Stationary (transverse) waves: formation, nodes and antinodes, node separation = λ/2.
Light in the EM spectrum; c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹; order of the spectrum.
Reflection of light; plane-mirror images.
Refraction of light: Snell's law n = sin i / sin r; dispersion.
Total internal reflection and critical angle sin C = 1/n.
Image formation by converging and diverging lenses: ray constructions, real and virtual images, magnification. [EXT] 1/u + 1/v = 1/f with 'real is positive'.
Wave nature of light: Young's double slit. [EXT] Δy = λD/a; diffraction grating d sinθ = nλ.
Sound as a longitudinal wave needing a medium; reflection, refraction, diffraction and interference of sound; comparison with light.
Audible frequency range; ultrasound.
Pitch, loudness and quality related to frequency, amplitude and waveform.
Noise; the decibel (qualitative); acoustic protection.
Charging by friction, sharing and induction; Coulomb's law F = Q₁Q₂/(4πε₀r²); 2-D vector addition of electric forces.
Electric field lines; E = F/q. [EXT] E = Q/(4πε₀r²); E = V/d between parallel plates.
Electric current I = Q/t; conventional current.
Potential difference and e.m.f.
Resistance R = V/I; I–V characteristics (metal, filament, diode); Ohm's law; resistivity ρ = RA/l; effect of temperature.
Series and parallel combinations of resistors.
Simple circuits: measuring I, V and R; internal resistance; effect of meters; potential divider.
Electrical power P = VI = I²R = V²/R; heating effect.
Domestic electricity: power rating, kWh and cost, live/neutral/earth wires, fuses and circuit breakers, ring circuit.
Magnetic fields and field lines; magnetic effect of currents: B = μ₀I/(2πr) (wire), B = μ₀NI/l (solenoid).
Force on a current-carrying conductor F = BIl sinθ; d.c. motor; force between parallel currents. [EXT] F = BQv sinθ.
Electromagnetic induction; Lenz's law; generators; eddy currents. [EXT] Magnetic flux Φ = BA cosθ; Faraday's law ε = −ΔΦ/Δt.
[EXT] Alternating current: r.m.s. and peak values (sinusoidal).
[EXT] Transformers Vp/Vs = Np/Ns; efficiency; high-voltage transmission.
X-rays: production, properties and uses.
α, β and γ radiations: nature, penetrating and ionizing power, deflection in fields.
Random decay; activity; half-life from graphs and data; background radiation. [EXT] N = N₀e^(−kt); decay constant k = ln2 / t½.
Detection (GM counter, count rate); radiation safety, the sievert.
Atomic structure; atomic number Z, mass number A; nuclide notation.
Isotopes; radioactive transmutation; decay equations.
Nuclear fission and fusion; chain reaction.
[EXT] Mass–energy relationship ΔE = Δmc²; 1 u = 931 MeV; energy released in nuclear reactions.

subject: physics
nameEn: The universe as seen in different scales
nameZh: 不同空間標度下的宇宙面貌

objectives.textEn: Hierarchy of objects (planet, star, cluster, nebula, galaxy); light year; astronomical unit.
Geocentric and heliocentric models; retrograde motion; Galileo's discoveries; Kepler's laws.
Circular orbits; T² ∝ r³; Kepler's third law T² = 4π²a³/(GM).
Apparent weightlessness in orbit.
Gravitational PE U = −GMm/r; orbital energy; escape velocity.
Parallax d = 1/p (parsec); apparent and absolute magnitude (qualitative); blackbody radiation; spectral classes OBAFGKM; Stefan's law L = 4πR²σT⁴; H–R diagram.
Doppler effect Δλ/λ₀ ≈ v/c; radial-velocity curves; rotation curves and dark matter; red shift and the expanding universe.
α-scattering and the nuclear model; limitations of Rutherford's model.
Photoelectric experiment and failure of the wave model; photon energy E = hf; intensity and photon number.
Einstein's equation hf = φ + ½mv²max; stopping potential; threshold frequency φ = hf₀.
Line spectra; energy levels E_n = −13.6/n² eV; electron volt; excitation and ionization.
Emission and absorption spectra; photon wavelength from energy-level transitions.
Wave–particle duality; electron diffraction; de Broglie wavelength λ = h/p.
Properties of nanomaterials; TEM and STM; Rayleigh criterion θ ≈ 1.22λ/d; applications and risks of nanotechnology.
Lighting: lumen, lux, efficacy (lm/W); inverse-square and cosine laws for illuminance.
Cooking: hotplate, induction cooker, microwave oven; efficiency and running cost.
Air conditioners as heat pumps; cooling capacity; COP = Q_C / W with Q_H = Q_C + W.
Energy Efficiency Labelling Scheme.

subject: physics
nameEn: Energy efficiency in building and transportation
nameZh: 在建築和運輸業中的能源效率

objectives.textEn: Rate of conduction Q/t = κA(T_H − T_C)/d; U-value; OTTV; solar control film.
Electric and hybrid vehicles; regenerative braking; efficiency of transport.

subject: physics
nameZh: 可再生和不可再生能源

objectives.textEn: Solar constant and solar cells; wind turbine P = ½ρAv³η; hydroelectric power; binding energy curve; fission reactor (moderator, coolant, control rods).
Environmental impact of energy use.

subject: physics
nameEn: Making sense of the eye and the ear

objectives.textEn: Vision: rods and cones; accommodation; resolving power θ ≈ 1.22λ/d.
Defects of vision and correction: lens power in dioptres (D = 1/f); near and far points.
Hearing: sound intensity level L = 10 log(I/I₀) dB; equal-loudness curves (phon).

subject: physics
nameZh: 非電離輻射醫學影像學

objectives.textEn: Ultrasound: acoustic impedance Z = ρc; intensity reflection coefficient α = (Z₂ − Z₁)²/(Z₂ + Z₁)²; A-scan and B-scan; depth = vt/2.
Fibre-optic endoscopy; optical fibres and coherent bundles.
X-ray imaging: I = I₀e^(−μx); half-value thickness = ln2/μ; contrast media; CT scans.
Radionuclide imaging: Tc-99m; effective half-life 1/T_e = 1/T_p + 1/T_b; gamma camera; radiation dose.
